data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: Receipt archive
data_stores.description: Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read/write orders
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.data_description: receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: Authentication status is explicitly uncertain: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because the card processor POSTs a webhook to it.
assumptions.basis: The source describes a POST webhook back to the storefront API, which indicates an HTTP application endpoint.

assumptions.assumption: The shoppers' trust zone is not stated.
assumptions.basis: The source describes shoppers interacting with the storefront but does not place them in a named zone.

assumptions.assumption: The card processor is placed in a separate tenant boundary because it is explicitly described as a third party.
assumptions.basis: The source says, "Our card processor is a third party."

assumptions.assumption: The shoppers carry credentials and personal information because they present email, passwords, session cookies and shopper identity information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API carries credentials, personal information and financial data because it receives shopper authentication and order data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that shoppers sign in through the storefront API and place orders through it.

assumptions.assumption: The order service carries credentials, personal information, financial data and business-critical order data because it reads and writes the order database and uses a worker password.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the service reads and writes orders, addresses and card-last-four, and that its password comes from an environment variable.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database carries personal information, financial data and business-critical order data based on its stated contents.
assumptions.basis: The source lists orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four as living in orders-db.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive carries financial and business-critical order data based on its stated receipt contents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that completed orders produce receipts in the receipt archive.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database is confidential because it contains shopper addresses and card payment information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains shopper addresses and card-last-four.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is confidential because its receipts record completed orders and payment-related order information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that receipts are written for completed orders.

assumptions.assumption: The shopper-to-storefront flow carries personal and financial data because shoppers place orders through the API.
assumptions.basis: The source states that shoppers place orders through the storefront API.

assumptions.assumption: The storefront-to-order-service flow carries personal and financial order data because it is initiated when a shopper submits an order.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.

assumptions.assumption: The order-service-to-database flow carries personal, financial and business-critical data because it reads and writes orders, addresses and card-last-four.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the order service reads and writes the listed records in orders-db.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt-writing flow carries financial and business-critical order data because it writes a receipt for every completed order.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order gets a receipt written to the receipt archive.

assumptions.assumption: The settlement webhook carries financial and business-critical payment-status data because it tells the storefront API that an order is paid.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the card processor sends a webhook to tell the storefront API the order is paid.
